amendments.body: The submitted diff does not implement tanksim-6e5.5.7’s required habitat/geometry scenario coverage. The only new test added is `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1`, and the code changes are limited to alkalinity-budget plumbing in files like `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229` and `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:533`. None of the bead’s required probes are present: there is no scenario-level test for biofilter scaling, light-depth behavior, habitat-specific fouling, substrate redox, or 1x-vs-2x equipment scaling, and there is no end-to-end habitat/geometry runner/report. As written, this change leaves the task’s acceptance criteria unmet and the intended habitat/geometry regressions unguarded.
amendments.rationale: This is a substantive correctness gap against the requested deliverable, not a cosmetic scope nit: merging this patch would still leave all of the promised habitat/geometry stories and the required e2e validation path unimplemented.

amendments.body: The new diagnostics still do not provide the habitat-specific failure output required by the bead. `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229` only records nitrification aggregate notes, and `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:533` prints whole-tank element totals; neither emits per-habitat biomass, colonizable area, or habitat modifiers through the tracing/debug path. That means even after these changes, a failing habitat/geometry scenario would not surface the per-habitat state the acceptance criteria call for.
amendments.rationale: The bead explicitly requires habitat-specific observability on failure. Without that data, future scenario failures will still be difficult to diagnose and the requested tracing deliverable remains missing.

payload.summary: Reviewing the actual diff in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7`, I found two substantive issues: the patch is off-scope for tanksim-6e5.5.7 and it does not add the required habitat-specific diagnostics. Targeted `tank_core` tests for the changed areas passed, and a full `cargo test -p tank_core` run still hits the existing `save_load_with_active_cycle_state` failure on pristine `HEAD` as well, so I did not count that pre-existing failure against this diff.
